primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease due to diabetic nephropathy

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control to meet NICE target <130/80 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends BP target <130/80 mmHg for CKD with proteinuria

medications.dose: 1.25 mg once daily, titrate up to 10 mg as tolerated
medications.purpose: Renoprotective effect and hypertension control in CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients

medications.medication: Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg PO with each main meal
medications.dose: 800 mg three times daily with meals
medications.duration: Until serum phosphate <1.5 mmol/L, then review
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107 recommends non‑calcium phosphate binders for hyperphosphataemia

medications.dose: 0.25 µg once daily, titrate to PTH target
medications.duration: Until PTH target achieved, then review
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107 recommends vitamin D analogue when PTH elevated

medications.dose: 500 mg IV single dose, repeat as needed
medications.duration: Repeat until ferritin >200 µg/L and TSAT >20%, then review
medications.purpose: Replete iron stores before ESA therapy
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107 recommends IV iron for CKD anaemia with iron deficiency
NICE NG107 ESA indicated for Hb <100 g/L symptomatic after iron repletion

medications.medication: Sodium bicarbonate 500 mg PO three times daily
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L, then review
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107 recommends bicarbonate for CKD with bicarbonate <20 mmol/L

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily, titrate to volume status
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate as needed, review quarterly
medications.purpose: Replace thiazide for volume control in eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 advises using diuretics appropriate to renal function for hypertension/volume overload

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect; opposite effects on potassium (ACE‑I may raise K⁺, thiazide may lower K⁺)
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine 1–2 weeks after starting ramipril; adjust thiazide dose or consider stopping thiazide
Monitor blood pressure and symptoms of hypotension after titration

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer can bind other oral medications, reducing absorption
interactions_checked.action: Take amlodipine at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after sevelamer

interactions_checked.interaction: No direct interaction; sevelamer only affects oral agents
Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma levels modestly
interactions_checked.action: 20 mg atorvastatin is safe; monitor for myopathy and LFTs

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect may cause hypotension and renal function changes
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure, serum creatinine, and potassium after initiating furosemide

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for sodium overload and altered electrolyte balance
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum sodium, bicarbonate, and volume status; adjust diuretic dose if needed

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 5; NSAIDs accelerate renal decline and cause fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Avoid NSAIDs; use paracetamol for pain if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium, calcium, phosphate, PTH, haemoglobin, ferritin, TSAT, liver function tests and full lipid profile are not provided – will be ordered before initiating ACE‑I, statin, ESA and iron.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, sevelamer, alfacalcidol, iron preparations is unknown – patient will be asked about drug allergies.
Current blood pressure reading is not recorded – assume BP above target and will be measured at next visit.
Volume status (edema, weight) not documented – clinical assessment required before titrating loop diuretic and bicarbonate.
HbA1c and recent glucose logs not available – insulin regimen will be reviewed after renal dosing adjustments.
treatment_summary: The plan adds renoprotective ACE‑inhibitor therapy, a statin for cardiovascular risk, phosphate binding, vitamin D analogue, iron repletion, ESA for anaemia, alkali therapy for metabolic acidosis, and a loop diuretic to replace thiazide in the setting of eGFR 6.7 mL/min/1.73 m². Existing amlodipine is continued. All additions follow NICE NG107/NG203 recommendations, with dosing adjusted for advanced CKD and close monitoring of electrolytes, renal function, bone‑mineral parameters, haemoglobin and liver enzymes. Contraindicated agents (NSAIDs, metformin, ACE‑I/ARB combo) are avoided. Monitoring and review intervals are specified per guideline.
